RouterSettings.description: The router's settings, as `settings/RouterSettings.java` declares them and as Gson spells them on the wire, plus `opt_changed_area_ms`, which the port adds because the Java constant behind it is inlined by javac and cannot be reached. Every field is optional: a value given here overrides the resolved default, and a field left out keeps it. Unknown keys are ignored rather than refused, which is Gson's behaviour and therefore this reader's.

algorithm.description: Which routing algorithm to use. One name is implemented; anything else is normalised back to it.

allowed_via_types.description: Let the router place vias. (The Java field is `viasAllowed`; `allowed_via_types` is the name Gson serialises it under.)

automatic_neckdown.description: Narrow a trace to neck_width_um where the full width will not fit.

copper_to_edge_clearance_um.description: Clearance between copper and the board outline, in micrometres. Applied to the board at load time.

enabled.description: Run the auto-routing stage at all.

failure_give_up_threshold.description: Skip an item on a later auto-routing pass once it has failed this many times. Absent (the default) retries every item on every pass.

fanout.description: The fanout pre-pass, which escapes SMD pins onto a routable layer before auto-routing starts.

enabled.description: Run the fanout pre-pass. It is skipped anyway on a board with no SMD pins.

end_via_diameter_mm.description: Diameter of the via at the far end of an escape, in millimetres.

fallback_to_board_vias.description: Use the board's own via rule when the configured diameters do not fit.

max_escape_length_mm.description: Longest escape trace the pass will produce, in millimetres.

max_items.description: How many pins one fanout pass may process.

max_milliseconds_per_pin.description: Wall-clock budget per pin. A machine-speed dependency: the same board can fan out differently on a slower host.

max_passes.description: How many fanout passes to run.

min_escape_length_mm.description: Shortest escape trace the pass will produce, in millimetres.

pin_sorting_order.description: The order pins are fanned out in.

ripup_allowed.description: Let the fanout pass rip up existing traces.

start_via_diameter_mm.description: Diameter of the via at the pin end of an escape, in millimetres.

timeout.description: Wall-clock budget for the fanout stage, as a timespan. A stage timeout is not a job timeout: the job still finishes COMPLETED.

hole_clearance_um.description: Clearance between copper and drilled holes, in micrometres. Applied to the board at load time.

job_timeout.description: Wall-clock budget for the whole job, as a timespan (for example 01:30:00 or 90s). Empty means no budget. A job that overruns it answers timed_out: true.

layers.description: Per-layer overrides, one entry per board layer in stack order. An array whose length disagrees with the board's layer count is discarded whole and re-derived from the board.

bend_cost.description: This layer's bend cost in millimetres of trace, overriding scoring.default_bend_cost. 0.0 is no penalty; 100.0 is the ceiling.

preferred_direction_horizontal.description: Whether this layer's preferred trace direction is horizontal.

routable.description: Whether the auto-router may use this layer.

max_passes.description: How many auto-routing passes to run. 0 means unlimited.

max_threads.description: Worker threads for the stages that are parallel. Defaults to a share of the host's processor count.

neck_width_um.description: Trace width, in micrometres, used where a full-width trace will not fit (see automatic_neckdown).

opt_changed_area_ms.description: Wall-clock budget, in milliseconds, for the pull-tight pass over a changed area. 0 or absent (the default) means no budget and the pull-tight always runs to completion, which is deterministic. The Java program hard-codes 1000 here and cannot switch it off, which makes its own output depend on how fast the machine is; set 1000 to reproduce that.

optimizer.description: The optimizer stage, which runs after auto-routing to shorten traces and remove vias.

additional_ripup_cost_factor_at_start.description: Extra rip-up cost applied at the start of the stage, decaying as it runs.

improvement_threshold.description: Stop once a pass improves the score by less than this fraction. (The Java field is `optimizationImprovementThreshold`.)

max_autoroute_passes.description: How many auto-routing passes the optimizer may spend re-routing what it rips up.

max_consecutive_failures.description: Give up after this many consecutive passes that improve nothing.

max_items.description: How many items one optimizer pass may process.

max_passes.description: How many optimizer passes to run.

max_search_steps.description: A deterministic cap on the total search steps the optimizer may spend; 0 means unlimited. Bounds runaway routing on incomplete boards without a wall-clock.

timeout.description: Wall-clock budget for the optimizer stage, as a timespan. A stage timeout is not a job timeout: the job still finishes COMPLETED.

trace_ripup_cost_factor.description: How expensive ripping up an existing trace is relative to routing a new one.

result_json.description: Where a run writes its result manifest. Read by the CLI; this tool answers its result directly and does not write one.

scoring.description: The routing cost table. The two per-layer arrays (preferred_direction_trace_cost, undesired_direction_trace_cost) are transient and cannot be set here: they are derived from the board aspect ratio and the two default_* costs below.

bend_penalty.description: Score penalty per bend in a finished trace.

clearance_violation_penalty.description: Score penalty per clearance violation left on the board.

default_bend_cost.description: Millimetres of trace a bend is worth to the maze search, where a layer names no bend_cost of its own.

default_preferred_direction_trace_cost.description: The value the per-layer preferred-direction costs are tuned from.

default_undesired_direction_trace_cost.description: The value the per-layer undesired-direction costs are tuned from.

plane_via_costs.description: Cost of a via that lands on a plane (a poured net), usually lower than via_costs.

smd_via_cost_factor.description: Multiplier on the via cost for nets whose pins are all surface-mount; 1.0 charges such nets the full via cost.

start_ripup_costs.description: Cost of ripping up an existing trace at the start of a pass.

unrouted_net_penalty.description: Score penalty per connection still in the ratsnest.

smd_via_relaxation.description: On a pure-SMD net, allow a via to attach to an SMD pad and cut the via cost to a tenth, even where the via rule itself disallows SMD attach. Default true keeps that relaxation; false leaves the via rule's own attach permission and cost alone.

strict_drc.description: Refuse a route that would leave a clearance violation, rather than accepting it and scoring the penalty.

trace_pull_tight_accuracy.description: How hard the optimizer pulls a trace tight; larger is more accurate and slower.

RouterSettings.title: RouterSettings

dsn_path.description: Path to a Specctra DSN file, or to a KiCad board JSON file. Exactly one of dsn_path and dsn_text is required.

dsn_text.description: The Specctra DSN document itself, as text. Exactly one of dsn_path and dsn_text is required.

dsn_path.description: Path to a Specctra DSN file, or to a KiCad board JSON file. Exactly one of dsn_path and dsn_text is required.

dsn_text.description: The Specctra DSN document itself, as text. Exactly one of dsn_path and dsn_text is required.

kicad_project_path.description: A KiCad .kicad_pro project whose board design rules (hole-to-hole, edge clearance, via minimums, netclass clearances, rule severities) are applied before checking. The CLI spelling is --kicad-project.

rules_path.description: A Specctra .rules file, applied to the board before checking. The CLI spelling is --rules.

ses_path.description: A session to import onto the board before checking (a .ses, or a KiCad session .json), so the report describes the routed board. The CLI spelling is --ses.

dsn_path.description: Path to a Specctra DSN file, or to a KiCad board JSON file. Exactly one of dsn_path and dsn_text is required.

dsn_text.description: The Specctra DSN document itself, as text. Exactly one of dsn_path and dsn_text is required.

output_path.description: Where to write the session file. When given, the result carries ses_path and no ses_text, which keeps a large SES out of the model's context; when omitted, the result carries ses_text and data (Base64) instead.

rules_path.description: A Specctra .rules file, applied at priority 40 and then re-read against the loaded board. The CLI spelling is --rules.

ses_path.description: An existing session to import onto the board before routing (a .ses, or a KiCad session .json), so the run continues from a previous result. The CLI spelling is --ses.

settings.description: A sparse RouterSettings override, applied at priority 70 above every other settings source. Call list_settings for the field names, their descriptions and the defaults in force. Only the fields named here are overridden.
